question: A patient presents to the clinic with symptoms of dizziness on standing up. He says it started soon after he was diagnosed with hypertension and started taking treatment for it. He has no other medical history. The physician decides to switch to another antihypertensive that does not cause orthostatic hypotension. Which of the following should be the drug of choice for this patient?
analysis: The patient is experiencing orthostatic hypotension as a side effect of the antihypertensive medication. Amlodipine is a calcium channel blocker that is less likely to cause orthostatic hypotension compared to other antihypertensive medications like alpha-blockers (Methyldopa, Clonidine) or beta-blockers (Propranolol). Enalapril is an ACE inhibitor and does not typically cause orthostatic hypotension. Therefore, switching to Amlodipine would be the most appropriate choice for this patient.
